sections.description: This section consolidates the core claims: a Chief Customer Officer is not universally required; its value emerges in environments with strong departmental silos, where customers move across multiple functional areas. The CCO's job is to bridge those silos and adopt a customer-centric view that spans operations rather than focusing solely on a single department.
sections.title: Key points

summary: Jeanne Bliss argues that a Chief Customer Officer (CCO) is not a universal solution for improving customer focus. The CCO is most relevant in highly siloed organizations, where departments such as billing, operations, and marketing excel within their own domains but create a fragmented customer experience across silos. In such contexts, the CCO (or Chief Experience Officer) acts as a unifying, cross-functional advocate—described as a form of human duct tape—whose role is to align silos from the customer experience perspective and ensure coordination across operations toward a seamless customer journey.
title: Do You Need a Chief Customer Officer? Not a Silver Bullet
